s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive, painless facial swelling with bony expansion
salient_findings: 3-month history of painless swelling in the right upper posterior tooth region
4.0×3.5 cm diffuse, well-defined, hard, nontender swelling on the right middle third of the face
Ground-glass trabecular pattern with radiolucency around the roots of deciduous teeth and erupting premolars on radiographs
key_facts: 9-year-old boy
3-month history of swelling
Painless swelling in the right upper posterior tooth region
Facial asymmetry
Unremarkable medical and family histories
4.0×3.5 cm diffuse, well-defined, hard, nontender swelling on the right middle third of the face
Normal overlying skin
Intraoral ovoid, hard, nontender swelling in the right buccal vestibule
Buccal cortical expansion and slight palatal expansion
No mucosal changes
Ground-glass trabecular pattern on radiographs
Radiolucency around the roots of deciduous teeth and erupting premolars
Expansion of the buccal and palatal cortical plates on cone-beam CT
Involvement of more than half of the right maxillary sinus

shortlist.label: Juvenile ossifying fibroma
shortlist.why_kept: Matches the clinical and radiological findings of a well-defined, hard, nontender swelling with a ground-glass trabecular pattern and buccal cortical expansion

shortlist.label: Fibrous dysplasia
shortlist.why_kept: Considered due to the presence of a ground-glass appearance, but less likely due to the well-defined margin and lack of ill-defined borders

shortlist.label: Cherubism
shortlist.why_kept: Possible due to the presence of bilateral facial swelling and bony expansion, although the case presents with unilateral involvement

shortlist.label: Central giant cell granuloma
shortlist.why_kept: Considered due to the presence of a jaw lesion with radiolucency and expansion, although the ground-glass pattern is not typical

shortlist.label: Cemento-ossifying fibroma
shortlist.why_kept: Similar to juvenile ossifying fibroma, but less likely due to the specific radiological features and location of the lesion

raw.rationale: The well-defined margin of the swelling and the ground-glass internal pattern on radiographs are characteristic of juvenile ossifying fibroma, which aligns with the clinical and radiological findings presented in the case.

rejected.label: Fibrous dysplasia
rejected.why: Ill-defined margin and merging with surrounding areas are typical of fibrous dysplasia, which contradicts the well-defined margin observed in this case.

rejected.label: Cherubism
rejected.why: Typically presents with bilateral involvement and familial history, which is not mentioned in the case.

rejected.label: Central giant cell granuloma
rejected.why: Often presents with more aggressive features and radiolucency, which does not match the ground-glass appearance and well-defined margin in this case.

rejected.label: Cemento-ossifying fibroma
rejected.why: Although similar to juvenile ossifying fibroma, the specific location and age of the patient, along with the radiographic pattern, more strongly support juvenile ossifying fibroma.
